title: batten.yaml
description: A project's procedural memory, declared as data: the phases it runs, the domains it fans out over, the checks that gate a close, and the ceilings an unattended run may not cross. The engine knows nothing about any project — it reads this file and executes it. Governing rule: if a hook cannot enforce it or a command cannot run it, it does not belong here. Over-declaring turns the spec into a DSL nobody maintains.

version.description: Spec format version. Only 1 exists; the loader rejects anything else rather than guessing at forward compatibility.

project.description: Project name. Namespaces runs in the store, so two repos sharing one batten.db do not collide.

unit.description: The work-item noun this repo already uses: US, ticket, issue, story. batten never invents one — it reads yours out of branch names and commit messages.

name.description: The noun itself, as your team says it out loud: "US", "ticket", "issue". Used in messages back to the agent.

pattern.description: Go regexp (RE2) that matches a unit id anywhere in free text — a branch name, a prompt, a commit message. Example: 'US-\d{3}'. This is how batten answers "which unit is this commit for?" without being told.

plan.description: Path to the canonical plan document that holds the unit blocks (acceptance criteria, tasks). Optional: repos that track units in an issue tracker instead of a file simply omit it.

locator.description: How to find one unit's block inside `plan`. '{id}' is substituted with the unit id. Example: '### {id}' finds the Markdown heading for US-034.

artifacts.description: Where each phase writes its output. Keys are artifact kinds (referenced from phases[].reads); values are paths relative to the repo root. Every path MUST contain '{id}' — without it every unit would overwrite the same file, and the loader refuses to start.

phases.description: The state machine, in order. The names are yours; the mechanics are batten's. Most real workflows are a variant of research -> plan -> build -> verify -> fix -> close.

domains.description: The fan-out axes — the only genuinely project-specific part of the file. One domain per area of the codebase that a separate subagent can own with a disjoint write-set. Keyed by domain name (backend, frontend, ml, db...).

gates.description: Verdict checkpoints, keyed by gate name. A phase references one via `gate:`. This is where the evidence rule lives.

budget.description:
The tripwire an unattended overnight run otherwise lacks.

On a subscription the marginal cost of a token is zero, so "dollars spent" is the wrong ceiling. Three honest ceilings replace it, and batten enforces whichever ones it can actually measure. A ceiling it cannot measure is reported as unavailable — never as zero.

tokens_per_run.description: Hard ceiling on total tokens for one run (all five buckets: input, output, 5m cache write, 1h cache write, cache read; parent agent AND every fanned-out subagent). This is the only thing that can be counted exactly, which is why it is the ceiling to trust. Underscores are allowed for readability (3_000_000).

imputed_usd_per_run.description: What this run's tokens WOULD have cost at API list price. NOT a bill — on a subscription nothing is charged. It measures the value being pulled out of the subscription, which is the honest way to compare a run against an API budget. Computed from batten's own price table, never from the transcript's total_cost_usd field (which is known to be wrong).

quota_pct_per_run.description: Share of the rolling 5-hour subscription window this run may burn, as a percentage. Anthropic publishes no absolute quota numbers, so a percentage is the ONLY trustworthy quota metric — an absolute token figure would be invented. Requires `batten statusline` to be installed, since the quota is exposed to the status line and to nothing else. Without it this ceiling is simply not enforced, and `batten budget` says so rather than reporting 0%.

max_iterations.description: How many times a fix -> re-verify loop may go round before batten stops it. The guard against an overnight run grinding on the same failing check until the window is gone.

on_exceed.description: What happens when a declared ceiling is crossed. `block`: the close gate DENIES the commit (the ceiling is real). `warn`: the gate says so loudly on the commit and lets it through. `downgrade_effort` was removed — it was accepted and never honoured, because lowering the model's effort is orchestration and batten does not orchestrate.

capabilities.description: Optional integrations. Every one of these degrades gracefully: if the provider is absent, batten falls back (graph -> grep) and never fails the run. Declare only what is actually installed — a declared-and-absent capability is noise that `batten doctor` will nag about.

graph.description: Structural memory: what the code IS, right now. Reconstructed deterministically from the AST — this is where a fan-out otherwise pays a large re-orientation tax (grep + N reads) just to answer "what already exists?".

provider.description: Code-graph provider. `none` (or omitted) falls back to grep — the spec degrades, it does not fail.

query_before_read.description: In phases marked `graph_query: true`, answer "what already exists?" by querying the graph instead of grepping and reading files.

lessons.description: Keep this false. graphify's outcome/lessons layer overlaps episodic memory, which engram owns and does better. Two systems claiming to remember the same decisions is how they drift apart.

memory.description: Episodic memory: what we DECIDED, over time. batten never builds this — it interoperates.

provider.description: Episodic memory provider, consulted before planning and written to after closing.

obsidian.description: The human surface. batten writes plain files straight into the vault — .md, .canvas, .base are just files. (The Obsidian CLI needs the desktop app running, which makes it useless from a hook or from CI.)

vault.description: Absolute path to the Obsidian vault. Point it at the same vault your code-graph exports to and the wikilinks between a run note and a code node will resolve.

export.description: What to write into the vault. `runs`: a note per unit with typed frontmatter. `verdicts`: the verdict envelopes. `canvas`: the run DAG as JSON Canvas 1.0, which Obsidian renders with zero layout code on our side.

compression.description: Context compression. Admitted, but measured — not taken on faith.

provider.description: Compression provider. Install it as a proxy (its own `init`), never in MCP mode: an MCP compression tool runs after the content is already in the context window and already billed.

memory.description: Keep this false. The provider's own memory layer would overwrite ground that engram already owns.

measure.description: Instrument it. batten already counts tokens per node, so it can prove whether compression saves anything in YOUR fan-out instead of quoting the vendor's benchmark. There is an open question about whether such hooks even fire for subagents launched via the Agent tool — and a fan-out is exactly where that would matter. If it does not save, turn it off with one line.

enforcement.description: enforce (default) denies; report turns gates into visible warnings — the adoption ramp.

id.description: Phase name. Yours, not ours — use the word your team already says ('research', 'qa', 'cierre'). Must be unique within the file.

optional.description: The phase may be skipped when it does not apply (e.g. a research phase only runs when the unit brings in unfamiliar technology).

interactive.description: This phase is a long human dialogue and belongs in its own session. An unattended run must stop before it, not attempt it.

fanout.description: This phase spawns one subagent per marked domain, plus one per parallel sub-task with a disjoint write-set. It is the phase the write-set guard exists to protect.

reads.description: Inputs: artifact kinds (keys of `artifacts`) or ids of earlier phases. The loader rejects a reference to neither — a phase that reads an artifact nobody writes is a typo, and it should surface at load time rather than at 3am.

graph_query.description: Answer "what already exists?" with the code graph rather than by grepping and reading. Falls back to grep when no graph provider is configured.

anchor.description: Record the base git SHA when this phase starts. Set it on the build phase. Every later phase then diffs from that anchor rather than from HEAD~N — which is what keeps the review scope correct when work interleaves, rebases, or lands on top of someone else's commits.

diff_from.description: Operate only on this unit's diff, measured from the recorded anchor. Set it on the verify phase so QA reviews the unit's changes and not the whole tree.

gate.description: Name of the gate (a key of `gates`) this phase must emit a verdict for. The loader rejects a reference to a gate that does not exist.

requires_verdict.description: THE HARD GATE, enforced by a PreToolUse hook rather than by good intentions. On the phase that carries this, a `git commit` is DENIED unless a verdict with this result — and a non-empty evidence[] — exists for the unit. Put it on your closing phase. Exactly one phase should carry it.

when.description: A free-form condition for entering this phase. ADVISORY and deliberately so: batten does not evaluate English. It prints the condition in the phase briefing at SessionStart, so the agent standing in the phase reads it and says whether it holds.

path.description: Root directory this domain owns, repo-relative, forward slashes. File ownership is resolved by longest matching prefix, so a nested domain (ml/agent/) correctly wins over its parent (ml/).

exclude.description: Subtrees carved out of `path` because another domain owns them. Without this, a nested domain's files would have two owners and the write-set guard would have to guess.

rules.description: Path to the AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md governing this directory. The domain's subagent reads it FIRST, before writing anything.

check.description: Commands that must pass before this domain's agent may declare itself finished. Take them verbatim from the Makefile / package.json — do not invent a command that does not exist in the repo. batten runs them; it has no idea what 'pytest' is.

coverage.description: A coverage floor for this domain, as a percentage. ADVISORY: batten does not measure coverage and does not run your coverage tool. It puts the floor in the gate phase's briefing so the verify agent reports the real number against it and can cite it as evidence.

skills.description: Skills this domain's agent should have loaded. `batten doctor` verifies each one actually exists — a renamed skill should be caught there, not fail silently in the middle of an overnight run.

agent.description: A custom subagent (.claude/agents/<name>.md) to run this domain, instead of a general-purpose one. The fan-out orchestrator uses it as the subagent type, so the DAG, the canvas and the hook matchers all show YOUR agent's name.

invariants.description: The rules a reviewer would catch and a distracted agent would break. These ride VERBATIM into every fanned-out agent's prompt, which makes them the highest-value lines in the whole file. Write them as flat imperatives ('session_id in every query'), not as essays. Mine them from your AGENTS.md files.

model.description: pin this domain's agents to a model (wins over the plan's tier)

checks.description: Commands that must pass at this gate. Their output is what the verdict's evidence[] cites — which is precisely why evidence cannot be hand-waved.

skills.description: Skills to run at this gate (a security audit, a code review). Their findings become evidence[] items in the verdict.

verdict.description: `required`: this gate must end with a recorded verdict envelope. A phase that ends with a summary instead of a verdict has not passed the gate.

evidence.description:
`required`: an approval must cite something. result="ok" with an empty evidence[] is REJECTED by the binary before it reaches the database, and the commit is separately denied by the hook.

This is the one failure batten exists to kill: closing a work item because it LOOKS fine. A spec that requires a verdict but not evidence is refused at load time — it would permit exactly the failure the gate is there to prevent.
